- We should avoid assignment of model IP. Instead offer a Limited Productization License (LPL) that grants ProspectCo the right to use, sublicense, and commercialize outputs derived from their inputs for specific product lines. Hi Emma — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Per our call prep, attaching Redwood's proposed response (orderform_legal_response_v1.pdf) and summarizing the path we recommend: 

1) Limited Productization License (LPL): we will prepare a short addendum (Exhibit A) that grants ProspectCo a narrow, non-exclusive license to use and commercialize Customer Outputs for specified product lines. This preserves Redwood's model IP while giving you the rights needed to ship your product.

2) Training / Do-Not-Train: ProspectCo can flag datasets/traffic as "Do Not Train." Redwood will exclude flagged data from model training and remove ephemeral logs from training stores within 90 days. We will provide cryptographic deletion receipts for flagged batches.

3) Feedback license & safeguards: feedback will be used only for scoped internal improvements or to service ProspectCo unless you opt into broader training. We'll include non-use commitments against competitors in the Exhibit.

4) Evidence & telemetry: we will deliver a redacted log excerpt and a one-page operational runbook showing how we tag and segregate ProspectCo traffic.

5) Commercial concession: we can offer either (a) a one-time credit applied to your first invoice equal to 15% of the first-year committed ARR, or (b) a 3-month pilot credit (full waiver of platform fees for the pilot). Ben has flagged 15% as our starting point for discussion; if procurement prefers a larger one-time credit, we can escalate.
